doc.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: Subbing with Thad Jones and Mel Lewis
summary: Roland Hanna sends him to sub in a band; a Brookmeyer piece with an open solo.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Well I had anxious moments like that. One time I sat in with Roland used to send me in to sub with Thad Jones and Mel Lewis. And that book is in tatters, it was then. He knew the book by heart. He’d been there forever after Hank. So, and he played this prank. He was a prankster in those days.

Oh God. Could you go in and sub for me tonight? I have to write some music for “The Today Show.” That sounded funny to me anyhow. I mean “The Tonight Show.” So I went in and I’m scuffling, and there was one piece, it’s either “Once Around” or “Three in One,” Brookmeyer. You’re going along, it’s a very abstract piece, and all of a sudden the band stops. Silence. And it says on the part “Play a solo.” No chords, nothing. Just play. And I had heard guys do that. And most guys like try out everything they ever knew, they go crazy. The record is — Hank is on the record. And what he played there is — you could play in any classroom. I mean it was so perfect, and the way he brought the band in. And I was pretty nervous about that, and stuff like that. Another time I wasn’t supposed to play. Okay he’s got to change the tape — oh ten minutes okay. Can you edit this stuff out?
